hints: Focus on what that pale yellow precipitate tells you, this is the classic iodoform test with alkaline iodine.
Recall that a positive result needs the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ in an alcohol or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ in a carbonyl.
Look for which pentanol contains a $\text{CH}_3$ directly attached to the carbon bearing the $\text{OH}$, that one can be oxidised in situ to give the precipitate.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the test**

That pale yellow precipitate is triiodomethane, iodoform. It is a very specific positive result.

$$\text{I}_2(aq) + \text{NaOH}(aq) \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3(s) \text{ pale yellow}$$

**Recall the structural requirement**

For alcohols, you need a methyl group next to the alcohol carbon. We call this the methyl carbinol group.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$$

**Why this group works**

Alkaline $\text{I}_2$ first oxidises this secondary alcohol to a methyl ketone, which then reacts further to give $\text{CHI}_3$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3$$

**Check the four alcohols**

Only pentan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It has $\text{CH}_3$ attached to the $\text{C-OH}$ carbon, so it gives the positive test.

options.A: Pentan-1-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, a primary alcohol with no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group. It oxidises to pentanal, not a methyl ketone, so no $\text{CHI}_3$ forms.
options.B: Pentan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and contains the required $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group. It is oxidised to $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ which then gives the pale yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate.
options.C: Pentan-3-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Although secondary, the $\text{C-OH}$ is attached to two ethyl groups, not a methyl group. Oxidation gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, not a methyl ketone, so the test is negative.
options.D: 2-methylpentan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Tertiary alcohols resist oxidation by this mild reagent, so no methyl ketone can form and no precipitate appears.
